title: Bridging two families of non-Hermiticity: from non-reciprocal couplings to an imaginary potential using the Lanczos transformation
abstract: Two types of non-Hermiticity found in physical systems, i.e., non-reciprocal couplings and complex potentials, have gained considerable interest recently. The former leads to the non-Hermitian skin effect, while the latter gives rise to a range of non-Hermitian symmetries such as parity-time ($PT$) and particle-hole symmetries. Although these two non-Hermitian forms have been incorporated in the same models, so far they have been treated as distinct families of non-Hermiticity. In this work, we establish an isospectral mapping between them using the Lanczos transformation. More specifically, we show that a generalized Hatano-Nelson model $H$ with non-reciprocal and spatially varying couplings can be mapped to a tight-binding model $H_L$ with real symmetric couplings and an imaginary on-site potential. This result holds even when the original $H$ already has an imaginary potential and exceptional points. Our work provides a refreshed understanding of the connection between different forms of non-Hermiticity. It also offers an approach to obtaining an intuitive physical understanding of exceptional points in $H_L$ that are elusive in $H$. Finally, our findings also warrant a versatile approach to constructing non-Hermitian systems with a complex potential and a real spectrum, without $PT$ symmetry.
summary: This paper introduces a novel mathematical technique using the Lanczos transformation to bridge two distinct physical descriptions of non-Hermiticity: non-reciprocal couplings and imaginary potentials. It demonstrates that a generalized Hatano-Nelson model can be mapped to an equivalent model with real couplings and an imaginary on-site potential. This provides a versatile framework for designing and understanding complex non-Hermitian quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper aims to establish an isospectral mapping between two distinct families of non-Hermiticity: those arising from non-reciprocal couplings and those involving an imaginary on-site potential.
main_result: The Lanczos transformation, when applied with specific initial vectors, successfully maps a generalized Hatano-Nelson model to an equivalent tight-binding model featuring real symmetric couplings and an imaginary on-site potential.
method: The core method is the bi-Lanczos transformation, adapted for non-symmetric Hamiltonians, which constructs an isospectral mapping between the two non-Hermitian forms.
model_or_system: The study focuses on 1D and 2D tight-binding lattice models, specifically generalizing the Hatano-Nelson model, which incorporates non-reciprocal couplings and potentially imaginary on-site potentials.
key_observables: The primary observables are the couplings (real vs. imaginary) and the resulting energy spectrum, which is shown to be isospectral between the original and transformed Hamiltonians.
important_parameters: The initial vectors $|u_0angle$ and $\langle v_0|$ are crucial parameters, as their specific choice dictates whether the resulting model has an imaginary potential or real couplings.
main_assumptions: The success of the mapping relies on choosing non-standard initial vectors for the bi-Lanczos transformation, and the method is shown to hold even when the original Hamiltonian already contains imaginary potentials or exceptional points.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the transformation on a 1D lattice, showing how different choices of initial vectors control the real/imaginary nature of the on-site potential and couplings. Further figures demonstrate the mapping in 2D (triangular ribbon) and the behavior of exceptional points.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the two non-Hermitian families, develops the Lanczos mapping technique using specific initial vectors, proves the isospectrality, and then applies this framework to construct novel non-Hermitian systems with desired spectral properties (e.g., real spectrum without PT symmetry).
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful mathematical tool (the Lanczos mapping) to unify the understanding of different non-Hermitian physics phenomena, which is highly relevant for designing and analyzing open quantum systems in optics and condensed matter.
